title: Cancer cells are no more selfish than normal cells; their self is smaller

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cancer cells are no more selfish than normal cells; their self is smaller

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Cells in a metazoan body are not less selfish than unicellular organisms or cancer cells; all are equally selfish, but the self that normal somatic cells defend is larger in space, time and complexity, its boundary being set by how far information passes between subunits.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: They are equally selfish, working only for the benefit of themselves, but the relevant self that they defend is bigger in terms of space, time, and complexity. As will be argued below, what defines this Self is the boundary of information being able to pass between the subunits.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Multicellularity vs. Cancer: The Shifting Boundary of the Self”. Scope: Somatic metazoan cells, cancer cells and unicellular organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-09: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.08

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim reframes whose interests cellular behavior serves rather than predicting a distinct observation. Information flow can be mapped, but it cannot establish equality of selfishness or uniquely identify the proposed Self.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Information-flow range and cooperative behavior could be measured, but describing all cells as equally selfish and assigning the beneficiary as the relevant Self is definitional rather than an independently testable consequence.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Selfishness and Self are redefined to make the statement hold.

The same data permit non-agentic descriptions.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.15

analysis feasibility: 0.12
discriminating power: 0.08

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The section defines the difference between cancer and normal soma as the scale of the self they defend. Connectivity and cell behavior can be measured, and those data look the same if one refuses the selfishness vocabulary. No result would count as a refutation that left the ordinary biology intact. The claim is a conceptual redescription.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Proliferation, migration, and gap-junction coupling are measurable. Calling cancer cells and somatic cells 'equally selfish' with differently sized selves redescribes those measurements and does not add a distinct outcome.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Selfishness and the size of a Self are not separately observable.

Any coupling-versus-dispersal dataset fits the sentence and its non-cognitive restatement.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.1
discriminating power: 0.08
data adequacy: 0.05
operationalizability: 0.22
